pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 12.4.1 CLASS READER: MAIN IDEAS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.4: Reading 12.4.1 Class Reader: Main Ideas

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Reading 12.4.1 Class Reader: Main Ideas
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why do people read story books?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify the main ideas in the section read in the text
2. discuss the lessons learnt from the text
3. appreciate the role of literature in fostering critical thinking

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Reading 12.4.1 Class Reader: Main Ideas

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Reading 12.4.1 Class Reader: Main Ideas

Teach
• Focus skill: identify the main ideas in the section read in the text.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Reading 12.4.1 Class Reader: Main Ideas.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Reading 12.4.1 Class Reader: Main Ideas
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do people read story books?
2. What is the importance of reading a short story?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
